# Solutions Notebook: Cleaning US Census Data (R)

Complete step-by-step solution code for the 22 extended data cleaning and EDA tasks.
### Task 1: Load Core Libraries

# Load packages
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
### Task 2: Locate Census CSV Files

# List matching CSV files
files <- list.files(pattern = "states_.*\\.csv")
print(files)
### Task 3: Ingest CSV Files into List
# Read each file into list
df_list <- lapply(files, read_csv)
### Task 4: Combine Data Frames
# Bind rows into unified data frame
us_census <- bind_rows(df_list)
### Task 5: Inspect Dataset Structure

# Structural inspection
glimpse(us_census)
head(us_census)
### Task 6: Drop Index Column

# Drop redundant X1 column
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  select(-any_of("X1"))
### Task 7: Clean Percentage Symbols from Race Columns

# Remove % symbols from demographic variables
race_cols <- c("Hispanic", "White", "Black", "Native", "Asian", "Pacific")
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(race_cols), ~ str_remove(.x, "%\\")))
### Task 8: Clean Currency Symbols from Income

# Remove $ and commas from Income
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(Income = str_remove_all(Income, "[\\$\\,]"))
### Task 9: Separate Gender Population Column

# Separate GenderPop into male_pop and female_pop
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  separate(GenderPop, into = c("male_pop", "female_pop"), sep = "_")
### Task 10: Clean Character Suffixes in Gender Columns

# Strip M and F suffixes
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(
    male_pop = str_remove(male_pop, "M"),
    female_pop = str_remove(female_pop, "F")
### Task 11: Coerce Character Columns to Numeric

# Coerce numerical variables to numeric type
num_cols <- c(race_cols, "Income", "male_pop", "female_pop")
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(num_cols), as.numeric))
### Task 12: Scale Race Percentages to Proportions

# Scale percentages to decimal proportions (0-1)
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(race_cols), ~ .x / 100))
### Task 13: Detect and Drop Duplicate Records

# Detect duplicates count
print(table(duplicated(us_census)))

# Remove duplicates
us_census <- us_census %>% distinct()

# Confirm removal
print(table(duplicated(us_census)))
### Task 14: Compute Missing Female Population

# Impute missing female_pop from TotalPop
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(female_pop = if_else(is.na(female_pop), TotalPop - male_pop, female_pop))
### Task 15: Median Imputation for Missing Race Values

# Fill missing race values with median
us_census <- us_census %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(race_cols), ~ if_else(is.na(.x), median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .x)))
### Task 16: Validate Population Consistency

# Verify male_pop + female_pop == TotalPop
us_census %>% 
  mutate(pop_diff = TotalPop - (male_pop + female_pop)) %>% 
  summarise(max_abs_diff = max(abs(pop_diff), na.rm = TRUE))
### Task 17: Reshape Race Columns to Long Format

# Tidy wide demographic variables into long format
census_long <- us_census %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(race_cols), names_to = "Race", values_to = "Proportion")

head(census_long)
### Task 18: Summary Statistics Calculation

# Calculate key income summary metrics
us_census %>% 
  summarise(
    mean_income = mean(Income, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_income = median(Income, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_income = sd(Income, na.rm = TRUE)
### Task 19: Visualize Income Distribution

# Histogram of median income distribution
ggplot(us_census, aes(x = Income)) + 
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") + 
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of State Median Income",
    x = "Median Income ($)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()
### Task 20: Visualize Race Proportion vs Income

# Scatter plot of Hispanic proportion vs Income
ggplot(us_census, aes(x = Hispanic, y = Income)) + 
  geom_point(color = "darkorange", size = 2.5) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") + 
  labs(
    title = "Hispanic Proportion vs Median Income",
    x = "Hispanic Proportion",
    y = "Median Income ($)"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()
### Task 21: Extract Highest & Lowest Income States

# Top 5 income states
top_5 <- us_census %>% 
  select(State, Income) %>% 
  arrange(desc(Income)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5)

# Bottom 5 income states
bottom_5 <- us_census %>% 
  select(State, Income) %>% 
  arrange(Income) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5)

print(top_5)
print(bottom_5)
### Task 22: Export Clean Dataset
# Export clean dataset to CSV
write_csv(us_census, "clean_us_census.csv")
